Evolving AI Offering Brings E7 to
Office Range
As part of several product announcements, MSFT today
introduced an E7 SKU to its Office line-up. E7 will combine the
E5 capabilities with Copilot and Agent 365, and represents a
clear up-sell opportunity. We like this move as it harmonizes
the fragmenting Office plus Add-On landscape.\xa0
The Office Suite is one of MSFT's largest franchises, with over 400mn users. Seat growth has
been one growth factor but upside here is limited (mostly entry level expansions), and hence
capturing greater value has been the more important driver of growth. In this respect, we like
the introduction of E7 today as it enables the continuation of MSFT's upsell strategy by bundling
more value into an offering at a higher price point. E7 should increase investors' confidence that
MSFT can maintain solid Office growth (currently around mid-teens level YoY) for longer. We also
note the launch of Wave 3 for MSFT Copilot which includes the offering of Anthropic's models
(beside OpenAI) and Claude\xa0Cowork capabilities and cements MSFT's role as a successful fast
follower of new technology.
When MSFT launched Copilot a while ago, many investors asked why it was not part of a new
SKU (E7 for example). At the time, it seemed MSFT wanted to make Copilot available to a
broader audience (not just the high-end SKU customers) and hence the separate pricing.
However, it does create friction in the sales process, especially for the enterprise level, if two
different pricing agreements\xa0(an Office SKU and the Copilot commitment) and discount levels
need to be discussed. In this respect, the new E7 offerings is just a natural extension. E7 includes
E5 plus Copilot and Agent 365. At $99 per user, the offering is above the $60 E5 price (price
update on July 2026) but is cheaper than the individual components (E5 $60 plus Copilot $30
plus Agent 365 $15). We note that in recent quarters, E5 was mentioned as the main growth
driver for Office growth, followed by Copilot.
With its product announcements today, Microsoft also provides an answer for another recent
investor discussion point around the evolution of work. When Anthropic launched Claude
Cowork a few weeks ago, we received many questions about MSFT capabilities to innovate on
its productivity offering and defend its position as the leading productivity suite provider given
the newer AI players and their offerings in the space. However, today's announcement of the 3rd
Wave of Copilot provides clear answers here. As part of the news, MSFT explained that it will use
Anthropic's Claude models but also more importantly some of the Claudework capabilities
(multi-step work). This confirms to us MSFT's role as a fast follower. The combination of the new
